title: DFS in Marrakesh: Find the Route First!
description: Watch Depth-First Search (DFS) “dive” through a maze-like street graph to reach the destination. This visualization shows how DFS explores paths deeply before backtracking when streets branch.
ig_caption:
🧭✨ DFS in a real street-grid—straight from the heart of Marrakesh (Medina)!

In Depth-First Search (DFS), the algorithm picks a neighbor and keeps going as deep as possible, then backtracks when it hits a dead end. On a graph built from real map intersections and streets, DFS uses a stack-like exploration order: each node becomes “discovered,” edges are traversed in a specific direction, and failure triggers systematic retreat to the last branching point.

📍Graph theory angle: your city streets become a graph G(V, E) where intersections are vertices (V) and road segments are edges (E). DFS is great for learning structure—especially for exploring connectivity and finding some paths quickly—but it’s not guaranteed shortest unless paired with extra logic (like BFS or weighted shortest paths).

🎥 Want to see DFS vs BFS on the same route? Comment your start/end intersections (or drop a neighborhood name) and I’ll generate the next visualization! 🚀
fb_caption:
How does DFS think on real city maps? 🗺️
Depth-First Search explores a street graph by diving deep along one route, then backtracking when it can’t go further—essentially a systematic graph search over intersections (nodes) and road segments (edges).
